tier_definitions.T5: Publication-releasable scientific claim after final release approval.

claims.text: The evaluated workflow separates proposal, execution, evaluator identity, decision, and evidence release; reflection is excluded from numerical claim evidence.
Under the white-box catalog, the semantic grader detected 48 of 48 declared corrupt traces and rejected none of four clean controls.
The mutable manifest-only integrity ablation detected 4 of 48 declared corrupt traces; both methods' macro and micro recalls coincide under the balanced design, giving a macro-recall gap of 0.9167.
A prior policy-attested NVIDIA L4 replay completed two connected real-MACE infrastructure iterations and rejected both.
The second L4 iteration crossed the frozen validation force-component-MAE improvement threshold but was rejected because the binary reproducibility constraint failed.

The first L4 iteration improved the validation force-component MAE by 0.053 percent, remained below the frozen 0.1 percent threshold, and was rejected; both the relative value and decision are derived from bound aggregate evidence.

The L4 replay used mace-torch 0.3.16, a candidate-only checkpoint, an H1-approved bounded energy/force label view, one optimizer step in each iteration, and a separately identified aggregate evaluator.

excluded_claims: The candidate MACE model improved scientifically.
The grader is robust to arbitrary or independently designed faults.
The grader guarantees general scientific validity or security.
The exact-equality mismatch was physically significant.
Four accepted clean controls establish a population false-positive rate of zero.
